title: X6 · Evidence wall: why did orders-db take 9 minutes to restart?
description: The postmortem team pinned logs and metrics to the wall. Put each piece of evidence under the write-path step it’s about, ignore the red herrings, then name the root cause.

problemStatement.overview:
**Postmortem, Wednesday.** Last night orders-db was restarted for a routine patch. It took **9 minutes** to come back because it replayed **38 GB of WAL**. Orders were down the whole time.

The team pinned everything they found to the wall: log lines, metrics, a few things that turned out to be unrelated.

**The board is the write path.** Each block is labelled with a step. Drag the evidence that’s *about* that step onto it. Read the evidence as you go; it tells a story.

Some evidence is a **red herring**. It’s real, but it has nothing to do with this incident. Leave it on the wall.

Then name the root cause.
problemStatement.yourTask: Match six pieces of evidence to the six write-path steps, leave the red herrings, and name the root cause.
yourTaskSteps: Drop the log line or metric that tells you what that step was doing.
Submit, then answer the root-cause question.
hints: Look for the step whose evidence is an ERROR.
The WAL is only deleted after something succeeds.
problemStatement.moat: Evidence cards on the write chain. Finale answer = sst-full.

platformSpec.passMessage: The wall reads left to right: writes fine, memtables freezing, flush failing, WAL piling up.

finale.prompt: Root cause for the postmortem. Why did the restart replay 38 GB of WAL?

options.label: The WAL disk was too slow
The SSTable volume filled up, so flushes failed and the WAL could never be trimmed
The memtable limit was set too low

finale.explanation: Flush failed with “No space left on device” on /data/sst starting at 01:52. Without a successful flush no WAL segment could be deleted, so 38 GB piled up, and all of it had to be replayed on restart. The WAL appends themselves were fast (0.4 ms fsync).

pieces.title: 01:52:03 flush: ERROR open /data/sst/000913.sst: No space left on device
pieces.blurb: Log line, repeated every 30 s since 01:52.

pieces.title: 01:51:58 bloom: wrote filter for 000912.sst (1.1 MB)
pieces.blurb: The last filter written before things went quiet.

pieces.title: compaction: L0→L1 skipped, no new L0 files since 01:52
pieces.blurb: Log line from the compaction thread.

pieces.title: payment-handler: GC pause 41 ms
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Red herring. That’s a different service, and 41 ms doesn’t cause a 9-minute restart.

pieces.title: postgres-replica: btree page splits 1.2k/s
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Red herring. That’s Postgres. orders-db is an LSM store with no pages.

pieces.title: orders-db CPU 34%
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Red herring. CPU was fine. This wasn’t a compute problem.

pieces.title: tls: certificate for orders-db expires in 19 days
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Red herring. Worth a ticket, unrelated to the restart.

pieces.title: order-processor: 3 retries on PUT (timeouts 03:04–03:13)
pieces.blurb: Client-side log during the restart window.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Red herring here. It’s a consequence of the outage, not evidence about a write-path step.
